question: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts is used to enter a new line in the same cell in a worksheet in MS-Excel 2010?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alt + Enter.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In Microsoft Excel**, if you want to enter **a new line (line break) within the same cell**, you can use the keyboard shortcut **"Alt + Enter".**
 
• It is important to note that for this keyboard shortcut to work, the **"wrap text"** feature must be enabled under the **"home"** tab in the ribbon.
 
• Once enabled, your text will properly display on multiple lines within a single cell.
 
• This is especially** useful when dealing with long strings of text** or when needing to create more readable lists within individual cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tab + Enter:** There's no "Tab + Enter" shortcut in MS Excel. These are two separate keys with different functions. The "Tab" key is used to move the cell cursor one cell to the right, while the "Enter" key moves the cursor one cell down.
 
• **Ctrl + Enter:** "Ctrl + Enter" is an Excel shortcut used to fill the selected cell range with the current entry. This means whatever value or formula you've just typed into a cell, using "Ctrl + Enter" will fill that into all the selected cells.
 
• **Shift + Enter:** In Excel, using "Shift + Enter" allows you to move up one cell. This keyboard shortcut is particularly useful when you need to navigate through the spreadsheet and add or amend data, but would like to move upwards rather than downwards.
